messages.author: f0c4c757f6cbcd73
messages.subject: trend dynamics in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi everyone,
                  I just read the unmarked pdf and the Dail and Madsen (2011) paper to find more about the model extensions that include pop dynamics.
I was trying to figure out how the number of recruits is distributed according to each model and I'd like to know if this is right:

G[it]~Poisson(gamma*N[i,t-1]) in the autoregressive model
G[it]~Poisson(gamma) in the constant model
G[it]~Poisson( where gamma=N[i,t]/N[i,t-1]) in the trend model and gamma therefore, is equal to the population growth rate.


Last, in which cases would you use a trend dynamics?. I'm studying and invasive species in the front of the wave (where I expect population dynamics will be exp growth) and far behind the wave (where the dynamics is probably more similar to one of the first two).

I'd appreciate your input!


Alejandro

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] trend dynamics in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Alejandro,

You are correct about the first two, but the "trend" model is 

N(i,t) ~ Pois(N(i,t-1)*gamma)

so gamma is the finite rate of increase (usually called "lambda"). If gamma=1, the expected value of N(i,t) is equal to N(i,t-1). Note that this model doesn't include the latent S's and G's.

Richard
